# Data Source: stripe_billing_portal_configuration

How the customer portal looks and what customers can do in it. `terraform destroy` deactivates the configuration, because Stripe cannot delete one. Stripe refuses to deactivate the account's default configuration (the first one created), so destroy leaves that one active with a warning.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_billing_portal_configuration" "default" {
  id = stripe_billing_portal_configuration.default.id
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

Exactly one must be set.

* `id` - (Optional) Unique identifier for the object.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `active` - Whether the configuration is active and can be used to create portal sessions.
* `application` - ID of the Connect Application that created the configuration.
* `business_profile` - The business information shown to customers in the portal. See [`business_profile`](#business_profile) below.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `default_return_url` - The default URL to redirect customers to when they click on the portal's link to return to your website. This can be [overridden](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customer_portal/sessions/create#create_portal_session-return_url) when creating the session.
* `features` - Information about the features available in the portal. See [`features`](#features) below.
* `is_default` - Whether the configuration is the default. If `true`, this configuration can be managed in the Dashboard and portal sessions will use this configuration unless it is overriden when creating the session.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `login_page` - The hosted login page for this configuration. Learn more about the portal login page in our [integration docs](https://stripe.com/docs/billing/subscriptions/integrating-customer-portal#share). See [`login_page`](#login_page) below.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `name` - The name of the configuration.
* `updated` - Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

<a id="business_profile"></a>
### `business_profile`

The `business_profile` attribute supports:

* `headline` - The messaging shown to customers in the portal.
* `privacy_policy_url` - A link to the business’s publicly available privacy policy.
* `terms_of_service_url` - A link to the business’s publicly available terms of service.

<a id="features"></a>
### `features`

The `features` attribute supports:

* `customer_update` - See [`features.customer_update`](#features.customer_update) below.
* `invoice_history` - See [`features.invoice_history`](#features.invoice_history) below.
* `payment_method_update` - See [`features.payment_method_update`](#features.payment_method_update) below.
* `subscription_cancel` - See [`features.subscription_cancel`](#features.subscription_cancel) below.
* `subscription_update` - See [`features.subscription_update`](#features.subscription_update) below.

<a id="features.customer_update"></a>
### `features.customer_update`

The `features.customer_update` attribute supports:

* `allowed_updates` - The types of customer updates that are supported. When empty, customers are not updateable.
* `enabled` - Whether the feature is enabled.

<a id="features.invoice_history"></a>
### `features.invoice_history`

The `features.invoice_history` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - Whether the feature is enabled.

<a id="features.payment_method_update"></a>
### `features.payment_method_update`

The `features.payment_method_update` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - Whether the feature is enabled.
* `payment_method_configuration` - The [Payment Method Configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_method_configurations) to use for this portal session. When specified, customers will be able to update their payment method to one of the options specified by the payment method configuration. If not set, the default payment method configuration is used.

<a id="features.subscription_cancel"></a>
### `features.subscription_cancel`

The `features.subscription_cancel` attribute supports:

* `cancellation_reason` - See [`features.subscription_cancel.cancellation_reason`](#features.subscription_cancel.cancellation_reason) below.
* `enabled` - Whether the feature is enabled.
* `mode` - Whether to cancel subscriptions immediately or at the end of the billing period. Possible values: `at_period_end`, `immediately`.
* `proration_behavior` - Whether to create prorations when canceling subscriptions. Possible values are `none` and `create_prorations`. Possible values: `always_invoice`, `create_prorations`, `none`.

<a id="features.subscription_cancel.cancellation_reason"></a>
### `features.subscription_cancel.cancellation_reason`

The `features.subscription_cancel.cancellation_reason` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - Whether the feature is enabled.
* `feedback_options` - The IDs of custom feedback options configured for this cancellation reason.
* `options` - Which cancellation reasons will be given as options to the customer.

<a id="features.subscription_update"></a>
### `features.subscription_update`

The `features.subscription_update` attribute supports:

* `billing_cycle_anchor` - Determines the value to use for the billing cycle anchor on subscription updates. Valid values are `now` or `unchanged`, and the default value is `unchanged`. Setting the value to `now` resets the subscription's billing cycle anchor to the current time (in UTC). For more information, see the billing cycle [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/billing-cycle). Possible values: `now`, `unchanged`.
* `default_allowed_updates` - The types of subscription updates that are supported for items listed in the `products` attribute. When empty, subscriptions are not updateable.
* `enabled` - Whether the feature is enabled.
* `products` - The list of up to 10 products that support subscription updates. See [`features.subscription_update.products`](#features.subscription_update.products) below.
* `proration_behavior` - Determines how to handle prorations resulting from subscription updates. Valid values are `none`, `create_prorations`, and `always_invoice`. Defaults to a value of `none` if you don't set it during creation. Possible values: `always_invoice`, `create_prorations`, `none`.
* `schedule_at_period_end` - See [`features.subscription_update.schedule_at_period_end`](#features.subscription_update.schedule_at_period_end) below.
* `trial_update_behavior` - Determines how handle updates to trialing subscriptions. Valid values are `end_trial` and `continue_trial`. Defaults to a value of `end_trial` if you don't set it during creation. Possible values: `continue_trial`, `end_trial`.

<a id="features.subscription_update.products"></a>
### `features.subscription_update.products`

The `features.subscription_update.products` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `adjustable_quantity` - See [`features.subscription_update.products.adjustable_quantity`](#features.subscription_update.products.adjustable_quantity) below.
* `prices` - The list of price IDs which, when subscribed to, a subscription can be updated.
* `product` - The product ID.

<a id="features.subscription_update.products.adjustable_quantity"></a>
### `features.subscription_update.products.adjustable_quantity`

The `features.subscription_update.products.adjustable_quantity` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - If true, the quantity can be adjusted to any non-negative integer.
* `maximum` - The maximum quantity that can be set for the product.
* `minimum` - The minimum quantity that can be set for the product.

<a id="features.subscription_update.schedule_at_period_end"></a>
### `features.subscription_update.schedule_at_period_end`

The `features.subscription_update.schedule_at_period_end` attribute supports:

* `conditions` - List of conditions. When any condition is true, an update will be scheduled at the end of the current period. See [`features.subscription_update.schedule_at_period_end.conditions`](#features.subscription_update.schedule_at_period_end.conditions) below.

<a id="features.subscription_update.schedule_at_period_end.conditions"></a>
### `features.subscription_update.schedule_at_period_end.conditions`

The `features.subscription_update.schedule_at_period_end.conditions` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `type` - The type of condition. Possible values: `decreasing_item_amount`, `shortening_interval`.

<a id="login_page"></a>
### `login_page`

The `login_page` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - If `true`, a shareable `url` will be generated that will take your customers to a hosted login page for the customer portal. If `false`, the previously generated `url`, if any, will be deactivated.
* `url` - A shareable URL to the hosted portal login page. Your customers will be able to log in with their [email](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/object#customer_object-email) and receive a link to their customer portal.
